text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said it is considering allowing the use of state bonds at its repo tender operations.

- The NBS also said it expected the so-called reference banks -- the eight largest players on the Slovak interbank market -- in July to resume following the agreement on obligatory quoted volumes and spreads.
- The latest privatisation decision by the National Property Fund gave the management-led group Slovintegra more than 50 percent control over Slovakia's sole oil refiner Slovnaft.

- The overall volume of liabilities that were not paid by their maturity is now estimated at around 200 billion crowns, of which claims worth some 120 billion crowns are already considered as clasiffied assets.

- Grafobal a.s., one of the largest central Europe packaging materials producer, plans to increase overall turnover by 15 percent in 1997. Grafobal's Czech plant in Slany should post turnover of 630 million crowns this year.

SME - Opposition parties on Tuesday again failed to pursue some democratic changes in parliament. The opposition has proposed adopting a law on minority languages, demanded also by the EU, and more opposition participation in the supervision of the state's secret service.

- Jan Carnogursky, leader of the strongest opposition party, the Christian Democratic Movement (KDH), said Slovakia had to improve its democratic standards as soon as possible to catch its last chance to be invited to the EU.
- The government plans to introduce regulations on wage increases saying salaries have been growing faster than labour productivity.

- Slovakia's largest savings bank, Slovenska Sporitelna, and the second largest commercial bank, IRB, have been expelled from the Prague Stock Exchange due to their minor trading activity and failure to pay membership fees.
PRAVDA - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar will answer deputies' questions in parliament on Thursday.
- Meciar said he insisted on the original timetable -- the first week of July -- for round table discussions including all parliamentary parties.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Confederation of Trade Unions (KOZ) have called on all political parties to start a dialogue on the social and financial problems of citizens.
- KOZ warned that several Slovak companies were near financial collapse and asked cabinet to start talks on this issue.

PRACA - The agenda of June's parliamentary session include a proposal by the ruling coalition to shorten parliament's term in the office by a few months due to the coincidence of municipal and general elections, both of which are scheduled for autumn 1998.
